common_name: Maraschino Salvia (Deep Cherry-Red Autumn Sage Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Maraschino bears especially large flowers in a deep cherry-red for this hybrid group.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun, and avoid overwatering, since this Texas-native-derived subshrub is prone to root rot in soggy or heavy clay soil. Maraschino bears unusually large, richly saturated cherry-red flowers for a Salvia greggii hybrid, opening in continuous flushes from spring through hard frost and drawing hummingbirds heavily throughout the growing season. Its compact, well-branched habit fits mixed borders, xeriscape plantings, and pollinator gardens, and a hard cutback in late winter keeps the plant dense and encourages the heaviest bloom. Extremely drought-tolerant once established, it thrives on lean soil with minimal supplemental water.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Salvia greggii cultivar trials

common_name: Lipstick Salvia (Bright Red-Pink Autumn Sage Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Lipstick bears vivid red-pink flowers on a compact, well-branched plant.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun, and avoid overwatering, since this Texas-native-derived subshrub is prone to root rot in soggy or heavy clay soil. Lipstick bears bright, vivid red-pink flowers in continuous flushes from spring through hard frost, drawing hummingbirds steadily throughout the growing season on a compact, well-branched plant well suited to a mixed border, xeriscape planting, or pollinator garden. A hard cutback in late winter keeps the plant dense and floriferous for the coming season. Extremely drought-tolerant once established, it thrives on lean soil with minimal supplemental water, making it a low-maintenance choice for hot, sunny Gulf South gardens.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Salvia greggii cultivar trials
